[ASSISTANT_SAID] Climate change has caused significant changes in ocean temperatures and weather patterns, leading to alterations in the distribution of marine life.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] As the ocean warms, several species are moving to cooler waters, leading to shifts in entire ecosystems and disrupting predator-prey relationships.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Ocean warming causes changes in sea ice, currents, and coastal upwelling, impacting marine life, particularly species dependent on sea ice.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Climate change leads to reduced dissolved oxygen levels, causing "dead zones" where marine organisms cannot survive and disrupting nutrient cycling.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Urgent actions are required to mitigate the impacts of climate change on marine ecosystems to minimize disruption to biodiversity.
